materials.title: NSS Field Operations Manual — Household Survey Enumeration
materials.extracted_text:
MINISTRY OF STATISTICS AND PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION
NATIONAL STATISTICAL OFFICE (FIELD OPERATIONS DIVISION)
INSTRUCTIONS TO FIELD INVESTIGATORS FOR SOCIOECONOMIC SURVEYS

CHAPTER 2: GENERAL PROCEDURE OF FIELDWORK AND DATA CAPTURE
1. Identification and Listing of Sample Units:
The primary sampling unit (PSU) in the rural sector is generally a revenue village (or census village), and in the urban sector, an Urban Frame Survey (UFS) block. The investigator must first visit the boundary demarcations of the selected village/block and prepare a clean listing schedule. If the population of the selected PSU exceeds 1,200 (or approximately 300 households), hamlet-group formation (rural) or sub-block formation (urban) must be carried out following the rules of equal population subdivision.

2. Respondent Selection and Non-Response:
Interviews should primarily be conducted with the head of the household or an adult resident capable of providing accurate financial and demographic details. In cases where the household is temporarily absent, at least three separate visits on different days and times must be attempted before declaring a non-response. Substitution of households is strictly prohibited unless authorized in writing by the Supervisory Officer according to the reserve list protocol.

3. Computer Assisted Personal Interviewing (CAPI) Standards:
Data capture on tablets must be validated daily before synchronization. Investigators must ensure that geo-coordinates (latitude and longitude) are locked at the doorstep of the dwelling unit. Any range check violation triggered by the CAPI software must be accompanied by an explanatory field remark in the designated text box.

materials.title: Handbook on Index Numbers: CPI and IIP Methodology
materials.extracted_text:
CENTRAL STATISTICS OFFICE (CSO)
METHODOLOGY NOTE ON THE COMPILATION OF CONSUMER PRICE INDEX (CPI) AND INDEX OF INDUSTRIAL PRODUCTION (IIP)

1. Formulation of Index Numbers:
The Index of Industrial Production (IIP) measures the quantum of growth in the industrial sector over a specified period compared to a fixed base year. The primary mathematical formulation employed is the Laspeyres base-weighted formula:
IIP = (Sum (Wi * (Qit / Qi0))) / (Sum Wi) * 100
Where Wi represents the weight assigned to the i-th item in the basket based on Gross Value Added (GVA), Qit is the physical production quantity in current period t, and Qi0 is the physical production quantity in the base period.

2. Mining, Manufacturing, and Electricity Sectors:
The industrial sector is broadly classified into three categories: Mining, Manufacturing, and Electricity. Manufacturing holds the largest weight (exceeding 77%), followed by Mining and Electricity. Data for the manufacturing sector is gathered from registered factories under the Factories Act, 1948 through the monthly production return system.

3. Base Year Revision and Splicing:
To capture structural shifts in the economy, base years are updated periodically. When a new base year is introduced, backward comparability is maintained through the Arithmetic Splicing method using a linking factor. The linking factor is computed as the ratio of the index in the new base year to the index in the old base year for a common overlapping period.

materials.title: MoSPI Technical Guidelines on Sampling Design & Variance Estimation
materials.extracted_text:
NATIONAL SAMPLE SURVEY DESIGN & ANALYSIS DIVISION
TECHNICAL GUIDELINES ON STRATIFIED MULTI-STAGE SAMPLING SCHEMES

1. Stratified Multi-Stage Sampling Architecture:
The standard sampling design used in NSS nationwide rounds is a stratified multi-stage design. The first-stage units (FSUs) are census villages in rural areas and UFS blocks in urban areas. The ultimate stage units (USUs) are households for socioeconomic surveys and enterprises for economic census follow-up surveys.

2. Allocation of Sample FSUs:
The total national sample size of FSUs is allocated among States and Union Territories in proportion to their population as per the latest Census. Within each State/UT, allocation between rural and urban sectors is made in proportion to their respective populations with a slight weight adjustment for urban sectors.

3. Probability Proportional to Size with Replacement (PPSWR) vs Circular Systematic Sampling:
In rural strata where census population data is robust, FSUs are selected by Probability Proportional to Size with Replacement (PPSWR), the size being the census population of the village. In urban strata, FSUs are selected by Simple Random Sampling Without Replacement (SRSWOR) or Circular Systematic Sampling with equal probability.

4. Design Effect (DEFF):
Because cluster sampling and stratification introduce correlation among units within the same cluster, the variance of survey estimates differs from simple random sampling. The Design Effect (DEFF) is defined as the ratio of the actual variance under the complex design to the variance under simple random sampling of the same sample size: DEFF = Var(complex) / Var(SRS). Investigators and analysts must report DEFF for key national indicators.

materials.title: Legal and Ethical Obligations under the Collection of Statistics Act, 2008
materials.extracted_text:
MINISTRY OF STATISTICS AND PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION
STATUTORY COMPLIANCE COMPENDIUM: COLLECTION OF STATISTICS ACT, 2008 (ACT NO. 7 OF 2009)

1. Statutory Authority and Scope:
The Collection of Statistics Act, 2008 provides legislative mandate to Central, State, and Union Territory administrations to collect socioeconomic, commercial, industrial, and demographic data. Under Section 4, a designated Statistics Officer is legally empowered to issue notices requiring individuals, business owners, and institutions to furnish returns within a specified time limit.

2. Absolute Secrecy and Confidentiality of Information (Section 9):
No information gathered for statistical purposes under this Act shall be used for any purpose other than statistical compilation. Section 9 explicitly mandates that statistical records cannot be disclosed to taxation authorities, police, or judicial tribunals as evidence against the respondent. Individual or identifiable data cannot be published without the express prior written consent of the informant.

3. Offenses and Penalties:
Failure to furnish information without reasonable excuse, providing intentionally false information, or obstructing an authorized statistical officer constitutes an offense under Section 15. The Act prescribes financial penalties and, for persistent failure, daily continuing fines. Furthermore, any statistical staff or contractor who breaches confidentiality or discloses microdata is subject to imprisonment and monetary fine under Section 20.

quizzes.title: Statistical Analysis: Index Numbers, CPI & IIP Methodologies

questions.question: Which index formula is primarily utilized in the compilation of the Index of Industrial Production (IIP) in India?
options: Laspeyres base-weighted formulation
Paasche current-weighted formulation
Fisher ideal geometric mean formulation
Marshall-Edgeworth composite index
questions.explanation: According to MoSPI compilation methodology, the IIP uses the Laspeyres base-weighted formula where quantities are weighted by base-period Gross Value Added.

questions.question: Which broad industrial sector carries the highest weighting (exceeding 77%) in the all-India IIP basket?
options: Mining and Quarrying
Electricity Generation
Manufacturing
Construction and Utilities
questions.explanation: In the Indian IIP basket, Manufacturing is the dominant component with a weight exceeding 77%, with Mining and Electricity accounting for the remainder.

questions.question: What statistical procedure is applied to maintain historical time-series comparability when an index base year is revised?
options: Harmonic normalization
Arithmetic splicing using a linking factor
Moving average subtraction
Exponential smoothing without adjustment
questions.explanation: Arithmetic splicing using an empirical linking factor derived from the overlapping period is the standard official method to connect previous and new base series.

questions.question: If the price index of commodity A doubles while quantity consumed drops by half under fixed base weights, how is the Laspeyres index impacted?
options: It drops by 50% due to reduced current consumption
It doubles for that item because Laspeyres uses base period quantities
It stays exactly at 100 because price and quantity offset
It becomes statistically undefined without Paasche correction
questions.explanation: The Laspeyres formula evaluates current prices weighted exclusively by base period quantities; current consumption changes do not diminish the base quantity weights.

questions.question: What is the primary weighting source for the items in the Index of Industrial Production (IIP)?
options: Consumer Price Expenditure Survey shares
Gross Value Added (GVA) contributions from Annual Survey of Industries
Customs import-export tariffs records
Corporate tax revenues submitted to CBDT
questions.explanation: IIP item weights are established based on Gross Value Added (GVA) shares sourced from the Annual Survey of Industries (ASI) for the base year.

quizzes.title: Sampling Design: Stratification, Allocation & Design Effect

questions.question: In the standard multi-stage sampling design of NSS surveys, what constitute the First Stage Units (FSUs) in the rural sector?
options: Individual household dwelling units
Census or revenue villages
Panchayat wards
Gram panchayat development blocks
questions.explanation: In the rural sector of NSS surveys, the primary or First Stage Units (FSUs) are census/revenue villages, while Urban Frame Survey (UFS) blocks serve as FSUs in urban areas.

questions.question: What sampling selection scheme is predominantly employed to select rural FSUs when robust census population data is available?
options: Simple Random Sampling Without Replacement (SRSWOR)
Probability Proportional to Size with Replacement (PPSWR)
Snowball sampling technique
Quota sampling based on land area
questions.explanation: Rural FSUs are chosen using Probability Proportional to Size with Replacement (PPSWR), with village census population serving as the size measure.

questions.question: How is the Design Effect (DEFF) mathematically defined in complex survey analysis?
options: Ratio of non-response rate to total sample size
Ratio of variance under the complex design to variance under simple random sampling
Product of stratum weights and household sizes
Difference between sample mean and population census mean
questions.explanation: DEFF = Var(complex) / Var(SRS). It quantifies the efficiency penalty or gain of the complex multi-stage design relative to hypothetical SRS of equivalent size.

questions.question: When the population of a selected rural village exceeds 1,200 persons (approx. 300 households), what protocol must the field team execute?
options: Abandon the PSU and substitute with the reserve list village
Conduct hamlet-group formation dividing the village into equal population segments
Interview all 300 households without sampling
Drop 50% of households chosen alphabetically
questions.explanation: Under NSS standards, large FSUs exceeding 1,200 population are partitioned into hamlet-groups of roughly equal size, and a subset is sampled to keep listing manageable.

questions.question: What allocation strategy minimizes sampling variance for an overall fixed sample size when stratum variances differ?
options: Equal allocation across all strata
Neyman optimal allocation
Arbitrary subjective quota allocation
Inverse proportional area allocation
questions.explanation: Neyman allocation assigns sample sizes proportional to stratum size multiplied by stratum standard deviation, mathematically minimizing estimator variance.

quizzes.title: Data Collection: Field Operations & CAPI Protocol Standards

questions.question: What is the required procedure before declaring a selected household as a non-response in an official survey?
options: Immediately pick the next door neighbor as substitute
Attempt at least three separate visits on different days and times
Leave a paper schedule in the mailbox and proceed
Mark as non-response after 10 minutes if no one answers
questions.explanation: MoSPI field instructions dictate that at least three separate visits across different days and times must be completed before classifying a household as non-response.

questions.question: Under what condition is an investigator permitted to substitute a selected sample household in the field?
options: Whenever the respondent appears uncooperative or busy
Only when authorized in writing by the Supervisory Officer under the reserve protocol
Whenever the investigator needs to meet their daily quota
Substitution is strictly never allowed under any circumstance whatsoever
questions.explanation: Informal substitution is prohibited; substitution can only occur via written supervisory authorization adhering strictly to the predefined random reserve list.

questions.question: What verification must be performed at the dwelling doorstep during CAPI (Computer Assisted Personal Interviewing) data entry?
options: Printing a physical paper backup
Locking GPS geo-coordinates (latitude and longitude)
Receiving an SMS OTP from the village headman
Calculating the full district consumer price index
questions.explanation: CAPI tablets must acquire and record valid satellite GPS coordinates at the physical dwelling entrance to audit geographical validity of enumeration.

questions.question: Who should be the primary respondent for socioeconomic household questionnaires?
options: Any minor child residing in the premises
The head of the household or an adult resident capable of providing accurate demographic details
The local postal delivery agent
The nearest commercial shopkeeper
questions.explanation: The head of the household or a knowledgeable adult resident familiar with family composition, expenditures, and economic activities must be the primary respondent.

questions.question: What must an investigator do if a CAPI application triggers a soft range check warning during data entry?
options: Force close the application and restart the device
Verify the value with the respondent and enter an explanatory remark in the designated field
Alter the respondent number so no alert is triggered
Skip the question without recording any value
questions.explanation: Soft validation warnings require confirming the unusual true value with the respondent and recording an explanatory supervisor remark in the designated box.

quizzes.title: Legal & Ethical: Collection of Statistics Act 2008 & Data Privacy

questions.question: Under Section 9 of the Collection of Statistics Act 2008, how can microdata collected from an individual respondent be used?
options: Exclusively for statistical compilation; it cannot be shared with tax or police authorities
Shared freely with commercial advertising networks to raise state revenue
Used directly by local municipal bodies to levy property taxes
Submitted as criminal evidence in magistrate courts against the respondent
questions.explanation: Section 9 mandates strict confidentiality: data gathered under the Act can only be used for statistical purposes and is legally exempt from search/subpoena by tax or law enforcement agencies.

questions.question: What is required before individual identifiable survey records can be disclosed to any outside party?
options: Approval from a local police inspector
The express prior written consent of the informant
Payment of a standard government RTI application fee
No consent is needed once the report is placed in parliament
questions.explanation: The Act strictly forbids disclosing identifiable informant records without express prior written consent from the informant who provided the data.

questions.question: What consequence does a statistical officer or contractor face for willfully breaching statutory respondent confidentiality under Section 20?
options: A verbal warning during internal review
Criminal prosecution with imprisonment and monetary fine
Transfer to another district office without penalty
Loss of one day of casual leave
questions.explanation: Section 20 classifies the unauthorized disclosure or breach of confidentiality by statistical personnel as a criminal offense punishable by imprisonment and fines.

questions.question: Which international benchmark outlines the professional integrity, transparency, and impartiality expected in government statistics?
options: The UN Fundamental Principles of Official Statistics
The Basel III Capital Adequacy Accord
The World Trade Organization GATT tariff guidelines
The Bretton Woods Monetary Exchange agreement
questions.explanation: The UN Fundamental Principles of Official Statistics (adopted by the UN General Assembly) is the universal ethical code governing impartiality and transparency in official data.

questions.question: Under the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act 2023, what privacy-enhancing technique is recommended prior to publishing research datasets?
options: Direct publication of full names and Aadhaar numbers
De-identification and anonymization (e.g. k-anonymity or aggregation)
Compressing files into password protected zip folders
Rotating column headers in reverse alphabetical order
questions.explanation: Anonymization and de-identification techniques such as k-anonymity and aggregation ensure statistical utility while preventing identity re-identification of survey respondents.
